sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Sashiko, whole cloth, and big-stitch quilting, taught slowly and sold as kits with the threads already matched.

sections.heading: Why slow
sections.html:
One needle, one thread, one running stitch repeated until the cloth changes. Hand stitching is the part of quilting that cannot be hurried and does not need to be; an evening of Sashiko goes about as fast as a pot of tea.

Everything here is built for that pace: patterns that fit on one page, kits with the floss cut, and workshops that end with fewer stitches than you expected and better ones.

sections.title: Workshops
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Small classes around one table, six seats, and no machine anywhere in the room.

items.title: Sashiko first stitches
items.body: The running stitch, the turn, and how to keep rows honest. Kit included.

items.title: Big-stitch hand quilting
items.body: Perle cotton, a hooped sandwich, and the confidence to stop picking out stitches.

items.title: Whole cloth marking
items.body: Drafting a repeating pattern with chalk and string, the way the old tops were set.

items.title: Boro mending evening
items.body: Bring one worn thing; leave with it patched and a thimble habit.

sections.heading: A workshop day
sections.html: Classes run three hours on Saturday afternoons. The kettle stays on, thimbles are tried until one fits, and the last half hour is always quieter than the first, which is the point. Finished practice cloth goes home with everyone, however far it got.

sections.title: Kits and patterns
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Printed patterns on one page, pre-washed cloth, floss cut to length, and a stitch guide that assumes nothing.

sections.heading: Shipping and shops
sections.html: Kits ship on Wednesdays in paper packaging. Quilt shops can carry the pattern line: write through the contact page for wholesale terms, and the wholesale box will include the sample stitch-outs for your counter.

sections.title: About the studio
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Opened after a decade of production sewing and one very quiet sabbatical with a needle and a grain sack.

sections.heading: How the studio works
sections.html:
For ten years I sewed fast, on deadlines, for other people's labels. The sabbatical was supposed to be a month off and turned into a winter of stitching lines on old linen at a speed my grandmother would have recognized. The studio opened the following spring with one table, six chairs, and the grain sack framed on the wall.

Everything taught or sold here was tested at that table first. If a pattern cannot be stitched in an evening and a half, it goes back to the drafting paper.

items.quote: I finished my first Sashiko sampler on the porch the week after class, and I have not watched television with empty hands since.
items.author: A workshop regular

sections.title: Commissions
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Whole cloth and Sashiko pieces made to order: a baby quilt, a wedding coverlet, a wall piece in your colors.

sections.heading: How a commission runs
sections.html: Commissions book about two months out. You describe the room, the occasion, and any colors that matter; I send fabric swatches and a marking plan before a single stitch goes in. The final piece arrives signed, with the leftover thread wound on a card, in case it ever needs mending.

sections.title: Write to the studio
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Wholesale terms, class questions, and commissions all land in one inbox, answered between stitches.

sections.heading: Open studio
sections.note: Bring a hand project or borrow a needle from the basket. The kettle is always on.
